title.narrative: Output 1.2. Increased institutional capacity of workers’ organizations

description.narrative:
The General Federation of Bahrain Trade Union (GFBTU) adopted recommendations to promote inclusion of domestic workers in social protection systems in October 2022. This followed a Regional Conference on Social Protection for Domestic Workers organized in collaboration with the Friedrich Ebert Foundation. GFBTU in different public statements promoted the recommendation publicly and announced its willing to discuss it as part of the national debate on the reform of social security systems in Bahrain, however, the exclusion of GFBTU form the Social Insurance Board of Directors and the Labour Fund Authority (Tamkeen) for more than three years is obstructing this effort.
The Federation, in collaboration with the Building and Wood Workers International (BWI), also updated its organizing strategy for foreign construction workers, the strategy that benefit BWI experience in working with migrant workers in the construction sector, was developed in January 2022. This is an evidence-based organizing strategy to outreach, mobilize and recruit migrant workers in the construction sector through the creation of Occupational safety and health (OSH) committees at worksite level. It will benefit the increasing interest in health and safety and assist GFBTU efforts to establish a sectoral union for construction workers, as a precondition to influence OSH policies at the national and sectoral levels.
Furthermore, the Federation developed a policy paper to promote the development of a national OSH policy. The paper was submitted to the government and employers’ organizations for discussion in a national tripartite seminar in November 2023 where it was recognized. The ILO supported GFBTU technically to develop a trade union policy paper on Occupational Safety and Health and conduct the national tripartite seminar to discuss its recommendations.
The ILO, through the FAIRWAY Project, provided technical assistance to the Federation to develop innovative strategies to organize migrant workers in the construction and domestic work sectors through enhanced cooperation with Building and Wood Workers International and the International Domestic Workers Federation
